mappings.note: Oxygen as the gas combustion needs is one of the conditions required for combustion, the query LO-33 names. Not LO-35, because a requirement rather than the flame is described.
LPG burning as rapid combustion sorts burning into its types. Not LO-35, because a class is named rather than a process explained.
The temperature at which a substance burns, its ignition temperature, is a definition within the combustion explanation. Not LO-33, which needs an investigation rather than a definition.
Picking the non-renewable energy source is classification of resources. Not LO-43, because nothing is conserved.
Excluding the substance that is not a fossil fuel is the same resource classification. Not LO-31, because membership rather than a property is tested.
The gas that supports combustion is a condition required for burning. Duplicate in substance of the earlier oxygen item.
Calorific value defined as the heat from a kilogram of fuel is a property of fuels. Not C-SCI2.3, which is cited only where the item asks for the unit of measurement.
The zone of partial combustion is part of the structure of a flame, LO-35's own example. Not LO-32, because no type of combustion is classified.
Coal burnt in a closed room giving carbon monoxide relates a danger to its cause. Not LO-36, because the hazard rather than an equation is the point.
Substances that catch fire being called combustible is classification by characteristic. Not LO-31, since no two materials are compared.
What can control a fire is fire safety applied in daily life. Not LO-40, which would need an extinguisher to be built.
The goldsmith's flame zone is the structure of a flame. Duplicate of an earlier item and coded the same way.
How calorific value is expressed is a question about units, and the frame's only measurement outcome, LO-37, covers angles alone. Cited at competency level for that reason.
Picking the non-combustible substance is the combustible/non-combustible classification. Not LO-31, because membership rather than a property comparison is tested.
What acid rain contains supports the acid-rain causal chain LO-34 names verbatim. Not LO-36, because no reaction equation is written.
Combustion releasing heat and light is the defining description of the process. Not LO-36, because no chemical product is named.
Suspended particles from coal causing disease relates a pollutant to its health effect. Not LO-43, because no protective action is proposed.
The chemical on a matchbox striking surface is the composition of a material. Not LO-33, because no condition for combustion is listed.

Methane burning with too little oxygen giving carbon monoxide ties a product to the incomplete-combustion condition. Not LO-36, because the causal shortage of oxygen rather than a balanced equation is the point.
A cracker's sudden reaction with heat, light and sound identifies explosion as a type of combustion. Not LO-35, because the item names a class.
Burning that starts without external heat is spontaneous combustion, another type in the same classification. Grouped with the explosion item.
Fuel efficiency expressed as calorific value is a property of fuels. Not C-SCI2.3, which is cited only for the unit itself.
The SI unit of calorific value is a measurement question with no learning outcome in the frame covering it, LO-37 being confined to angles.
The middle zone as the zone of partial combustion is the structure of a flame. Grouped with the other flame-zone items.
The colour of the outer zone describes the flame's structure. Grouped with the other flame-zone items.
The factors essential to ignite a fire are the conditions required for combustion, named verbatim in LO-33. Not LO-42, because no fire is being controlled.
What should be done to control a fire is fire safety in practice. Not LO-33, which covers what is needed to start one rather than to stop it.
Knowing when water must not be used on a fire is practical fire safety. Not LO-34, because the item prescribes rather than explains.
What must not be used on an electrical fire is again practical fire safety. Grouped with the other extinguisher items.
Which fuels run automobiles is everyday knowledge of where fuels are used. Not LO-43, because no pollution judgement is asked for.
Burning magnesium ribbon giving magnesium oxide is a metal-air reaction product, LO-36's own territory. Not LO-35, because a product rather than the flame is asked.
Charcoal burning in air giving carbon dioxide is a reaction product. Grouped with the magnesium item.
Combustion being a reaction with oxygen is the defining explanation of the process. Not LO-33, because it states what combustion is rather than what it needs.
Fuels being solid, liquid or gaseous sorts them by state. Not LO-31, because classes rather than a property comparison are involved.
Food as the body's fuel applies the idea of combustion to everyday life. Not LO-32, because the item extends the concept rather than sorting fuels.
Combustion described as a chemical process explains what it is. Duplicate in substance of the definition items.
Picking the combustible substance is the combustible/non-combustible classification. Mirror of the non-combustible item.
The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire defines ignition temperature. Duplicate in substance of the earlier definition items.
Comparing substances to find the lower ignition temperature ranks materials on a property. Not LO-35, which is used for the definition rather than the comparison.
Water preventing paper from reaching its ignition temperature relates an outcome to its cause. Not LO-33, because the pupil recalls the reason rather than conducting the investigation.
